convert_table-field: NOT AVAILABLE - this operation is intentionally withheld on this surface. IRREVERSIBLE. A convert emptied all 6,536 values in the column it declared required, returning 200 with notNull true (deploy#850 defect 5). It is the one verb that destroys data while reporting the opposite. Do it in the Teable UI on the tailnet with an export in hand, and read the column back before trusting the response. Use list_table-field instead. Calling this tool always fails and reaches no upstream.
create_record: Answers creation requests like file an issue or add a comment row linked to an issue by creating a new row. Existing choice questions belong to list_table-field.
create_table-field: NOT AVAILABLE - this operation is intentionally withheld on this surface. Teable accepts unknown field properties and silently discards them (deploy#850 defect 1), so a schema this surface appeared to create would not be the schema stored. Create fields in the Teable UI on the tailnet, then read back what was actually stored. Use list_table-field instead. Calling this tool always fails and reaches no upstream.
delete_record: NOT AVAILABLE - this operation is intentionally withheld on this surface. Teable has no archive verb for a record, so a delete is unrecoverable outside a restic PVC restore. This surface is additive and corrective only: correct a row in place, or set its state field to closed. Use edit_record instead. Calling this tool always fails and reaches no upstream.
edit_record: Answers update requests for an existing issue or comment row by record id, such as closing, retitling, or changing priority. Confirmation after a write belongs to get_record.
edit_table-field: NOT AVAILABLE - this operation is intentionally withheld on this surface. PATCH on a field returns 200, validates nothing and applies nothing (deploy#850 defect 3). A formula can be corrected, report success, and keep running the old logic. Convert in the Teable UI on the tailnet, then confirm what was stored. Use list_table-field instead. Calling this tool always fails and reaches no upstream.
get_record: Answers requests for a specific issue or comment row by table id and record id, including linked comment ids. Updates to that row go to edit_record.
list_base: Answers which bases are available, what their ids and names are, and which base is the tracker. Table discovery belongs to list_base-table.
list_base-table: Answers what tables exist in a base and what the issues table id is by returning table ids and names. Column and field discovery is owned by list_table-field.
list_record: List records from one table. `search` is the ONLY filter that reaches this surface, and it is a three-element tuple [term, fieldId, "true"]. The third element MUST be the string "true" to filter. Any other value, and the two-element form, return the unfiltered head of the table, indistinguishable from a filter that matched everything. searchHitIndex does not catch that: it is populated only when the searched field is among the returned fields, so any projection omitting it reads null on a filter that ran correctly. Negative-control with a nonsense term that must return zero rows, or put the searched field in the projection. Matching is case-insensitive substring scoped to the single field named by fieldId, which comes from list_table-field. `filter`, `filterByTql` and `orderBy` take JSON or TQL braces, and reach upstream only on an image built against umbra v0.196.0 or later, where the metachar gate stopped rejecting `{` in query values. An older image refuses them with a policy error naming the brace (mcp-beaver#6930). In TQL, LIKE is EXACT EQUALITY: neither % nor * is a wildcard, so `{title} LIKE "%term%"` returns zero rows with a 200 and no warning. Use `search` for substring matching and `filterByTql` for equality, comparison and boolean composition. Pass projection to bound the payload, and page with take and skip.
list_table-field: Answers what columns a table has, what its field ids are, and which choices exist for state, priority, or roles. Row search questions go to list_record.
list_table-view: Answers what saved views a table has and what a view id is by returning view ids and names. Row listing and search questions belong to list_record.
mcp_beaver_info: Report this MCP server's identity, mode, and served tool inventory. Read-only, reaches no upstream, and doubles as a liveness probe now that the protocol ping is gone.
